title: Writing Equations for Vertically Shifted Parabolas
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = x^2 (vertex at the origin, opening upward) is shifted vertically to two new positions: Position (a) has its vertex at (0, 3), and Position (b) has its vertex at (0, -5). Write the equation for each new graph.

steps.title: Recall the Vertical Shift Rule for y = f(x)
steps.explanation: Adding a constant k to f(x) shifts the graph vertically upward by k units if k > 0 and downward by |k| units if k < 0.
steps.why: Vertical translation adds k directly to every y-coordinate on the graph.

steps.title: Write the Equation for Position (a)
steps.explanation: Position (a) moves the vertex from (0, 0) up 3 units to (0, 3), so k = 3 and the equation is y = x^2 + 3.
steps.why: Adding 3 increases every output value by 3, placing the minimum at (0, 3).

steps.title: Write the Equation for Position (b)
steps.explanation: Position (b) moves the vertex from (0, 0) down 5 units to (0, -5), so k = -5 and the equation is y = x^2 - 5.
steps.why: Subtracting 5 decreases every output value by 5, placing the minimum at (0, -5).
